title: Unpaid-invoice follow-up and order-status desk
goal: Chase unpaid invoices on WhatsApp every morning, politely at first and firmer after a week, and answer customers who ask where their order is in English or Hindi.

agents.name: Collections follow-up
agents.description: Drafts a short, polite payment reminder for each overdue invoice.
agents.systemPrompt: You write payment reminders for a small business. Be polite in the first reminder and firmer after seven days overdue. Always state the invoice number, amount and due date. Never threaten, never invent a due date, and never promise a discount.

agents.name: Order-status desk
agents.description: Answers where-is-my-order questions in English or Hindi.
agents.systemPrompt: You answer order-status questions for a small business. Reply in the language the customer wrote in (English or Hindi). Only state what the order system tells you; if you cannot find the order, say so and offer to pass it to a person.

procedures.name: Escalating reminder ladder
steps: Day 1 overdue: friendly reminder with the invoice attached.
Day 7 overdue: firmer reminder, ask for a payment date.
Day 14 overdue: stop and hand the customer to a person.

workflows.name: Morning invoice chase
workflows.sampleInput: Invoice INV-2041, Sharma Traders, 18,500 rupees, 9 days overdue.

knowledge.name: Customer ledger notes and payment terms

sources.hint: Upload your payment-terms sheet and any customer-specific arrangements.

secrets.name: TALLY_API_KEY
secrets.why: Lets the follow-up read your overdue invoices. Read-only.
secrets.obtainAt: Your accounting software, under API access.

secrets.name: WHATSAPP_TOKEN
secrets.why: Lets the envoy send WhatsApp messages from your business number.
secrets.obtainAt: Meta Business Manager, under your WhatsApp Business account.

cases.rubric: Polite, states invoice number, amount and due date, no threat.
Firmer tone, asks for a payment date, still no threat.
Declines to send another reminder and hands over to a person.

cases.input: Customer says they already paid last week.
cases.rubric: Apologises, asks for the payment reference, does not insist.

narrative.whyAgentic: Each reminder has to read the customer's history and pick the right tone, which a fixed template cannot do. A person should still approve the first messages until you trust the wording.

a1.why: Writes each reminder in the right tone for how overdue the invoice is.
a1.tune: If reminders sound too soft or too stern, edit the system prompt in the Workbench.
a1.proof: The eval set below scores tone on four sample invoices.

a2.why: Answers order-status questions so you do not have to.
a2.tune: If it answers in the wrong language, tighten the language line in the system prompt.
a2.proof: Rehearse it as the busy shop owner persona and read the transcript.

w1.why: Runs the chase every morning so nobody has to remember.
w1.tune: Change the schedule on the trigger node in the workflow editor.
w1.proof: Run it now with the sample invoice and read what would be sent.

w1.n1.why: Starts the chase once a day.
w1.n1.tune: Edit the schedule on this node.
w1.n1.proof: The workflow shows a run every morning.

w1.n2.why: Reads the list of overdue invoices from your accounts.
w1.n2.tune: Change the URL or the status filter on this node.
w1.n2.proof: The trace shows the invoices it found.

w1.n3.why: Hands each overdue invoice to the collections agent.
w1.n3.tune: Pick a different agent on this node.
w1.n3.proof: The trace shows the drafted message.

w1.n4.why: Sending a message to a customer cannot be taken back, so it asks you first.
w1.n4.tune: Edit the message channel on this node.
w1.n4.proof: Each send shows up in your approvals queue.

m1.why: Connects the envoy to WhatsApp Business.
m1.tune: Reconnect it from the MCP tools page if messages stop.
m1.proof: A test message arrives on your own number.

k1.why: Holds your payment terms so the wording matches what you agreed.
k1.tune: Upload a newer terms sheet from the Knowledge page.
k1.proof: Answers quote your terms rather than guessing.

s1.why: The key to read your overdue invoices.
s1.tune: Rotate it on the Secrets page.
s1.proof: The fetch step returns invoices instead of an error.

s2.why: The key to send from your WhatsApp number.
s2.tune: Rotate it on the Secrets page.

p1.why: Your own escalation ladder, written down so the agent follows it.
p1.tune: Edit the steps in the procedure.

c1.why: Lets customers ask about orders directly on WhatsApp.
c1.tune: Bind it to a different agent from the Channels page.
